summary: Nigeria handles short tourist and business visits through its official e-Visa, applied for online before travel; the UK Foreign Office says visa on arrival is no longer available. The Nigeria Immigration Service says the tourism visa is for citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member states and countries with which Nigeria has visa abolition or waiver agreements.

declarations.text: In response to the Ebola outbreak, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control says travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete the free online Nigeria Health Declaration Form before boarding, and that passengers from all other countries are exempt at this time. The confirmation (PDF with QR code) is shown to port health officers on arrival.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says possession or use of illegal drugs, including cannabis, carries severe penalties, with long jail sentences and heavy fines also for smuggling and when transiting.
It is illegal to export African art, particularly antiques, without written authorisation from the Department of Antiquities, according to the UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada.

The UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada say it is illegal to import beer, mineral water, soft drinks, sparkling wine, fruits, vegetables, cereals, eggs, textile fabrics, jewellery or precious metals.

payments.text: The Government of Canada describes Nigeria's economy as cash-based: US dollars are widely accepted, ATMs are not widely available outside major cities, and credit cards are accepted at some major hotels in Abuja and Lagos — though it advises avoiding credit and debit cards because of the high potential for fraud. The UK Foreign Office warns of a spike in crime around banks and ATMs.

safety.text: Risk varies sharply by state. The FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara states and to the riverine areas of the Niger Delta, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east, because of terrorism, banditry and kidnapping.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The Government of Canada says the rainy season runs from May to October, with flash and seasonal flooding that can make roads impassable. The dry season, November to April, brings periodic heat waves well above 40°C, especially in central and northern Nigeria, and the dusty Harmattan wind, typically November to March and strongest from December to February, which reduces visibility and air quality.

tips.text: Apply for the e-Visa only through the Nigeria Immigration Service's official portal, evisa.immigration.gov.ng, linked from immigration.gov.ng.

Check advice for each state on your route, not just the national rating: the UK Foreign Office advises against all or all but essential travel to parts of the North East, North West, North Central, South East and South South regions. It also advises limiting travel after dark outside city centres, and the Government of Canada advises avoiding all unnecessary travel after dark.
Complete the free digital Landing Card before you fly and the Exit Card before you leave, on the Nigeria Immigration Service portal — travellers who do not can be refused entry or departure.

Take extra care when withdrawing or changing money: the UK Foreign Office reports a spike in criminal activity around banks and ATMs, especially at night, and says credit card fraud is common, so keep your card in sight when paying.
Carry your yellow fever certificate: the UK Foreign Office says you need one to enter Nigeria, except infants aged 8 months or younger and adults aged 61 or older.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nigeria?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you are exempt. The Nigeria Immigration Service says the tourism visa is for citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member states and countries with which Nigeria has visa abolition or waiver agreements; short tourist and business visits are applied for online through the e-Visa. No official page we could read lists the countries with such agreements.

faq.question: Does Nigeria still issue visas on arrival?
faq.answer: No. The UK Foreign Office says visa on arrival is no longer available and that all visa applications must be submitted through the online portal before travel.

faq.question: How long does the Nigeria e-Visa take?
faq.answer: The Nigeria Immigration Service does not publish a processing time for the e-Visa, and no official source states one.

faq.question: Can US citizens get a Nigeria e-Visa?
faq.answer: Yes — US passport holders are eligible for the e-Visa for tourism or business, applying online at evisa.immigration.gov.ng.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Nigeria?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Nigeria; only infants aged 8 months or younger and adults aged 61 or older are exempt.

faq.question: What is the Nigeria Landing Card?
faq.answer: A free digital arrival/departure declaration run by the Nigeria Immigration Service since May 2025. Foreign visitors (not transit passengers) complete the Landing Card online before arrival and an Exit Card before departure; those who do not can be refused entry or departure at immigration checkpoints.
